crop.notes: Long sporting column (gymnastics, turf, general notes); the Allen item is the last paragraph (crop-4/5), reprinted from the Washington Post.

ocr.notes: Gist readable; the Allen paragraph has many character errors (e.g. 'fom Aijen', 'Juarley Davis').

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican, reprinting the Washington Post, reported that Tom Allen and Charley Davis were matched for £200 and the championship, with Allen the 6-to-4 favorite after his win over Gilbert Tompkins.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republican: St. Louis, Sunday Morning, March 3, 1878, page 8. Item credited to the Washington Post.

facts.fact: A prize fight was arranged between Allen, 'the champion of America,' and Charley Davis at catch weights under the new London prize-ring rules, for £200 and the championship
Allen had earlier beaten the giant Gilbert Tompkins in England

notes: Paper said Davis was considered the best man in England since Jem Mace left for the antipodes; Allen favored at six to four.
